normalizedContentIdentity.inputContract: rawText is the exact extracted candidate string. Its JavaScript String value is normalized; no parsing, decoding, fetching, or URL canonicalization occurs.
normalizedContentIdentity.unicodeHandling: Apply ECMAScript String.prototype.normalize with NFKC exactly once before all other transformations.
normalizedContentIdentity.caseHandling: Preserve case. A lowercase comparison copy used by historical diagnostics is not the normalized-content automatic-match identity.
normalizedContentIdentity.lineEndingHandling: Replace CRLF and lone CR with LF; the later Unicode-whitespace collapse converts every remaining whitespace run, including LF, to one ASCII space.
normalizedContentIdentity.whitespaceHandling: Trim leading and trailing whitespace, then replace each ECMAScript Unicode /\s+/gu run with one U+0020 SPACE.
normalizedContentIdentity.punctuationHandling: Preserve punctuation, numbers, negation, named entities, attribution, emoji, and symbols after NFKC; do not strip or rewrite them.
normalizedContentIdentity.urlHandling: Preserve URLs byte-for-byte after NFKC and whitespace normalization; do not lowercase, decode, resolve, remove parameters, or follow redirects.
normalizedContentIdentity.hashInput: The exact UTF-8 bytes, without BOM or terminal newline insertion, of the normalized JavaScript string.
normalizedContentIdentity.retention: normalized content may be retained only in approved private evidence storage after source-terms, licensing, and privacy review; canonical/public records must retain normalizationVersion and normalizedContentHash even when normalized text is not retained
normalizedContentIdentity.automaticMatchRequirement: Both records must have normalizationVersion exactly equal to crucix-session15-conservative-normalization/v1 and normalizedContentHash exactly equal. A hash match under a missing or different version is not an automatic match.

clustering.candidateIdentityRetention: Every raw candidate remains immutable and addressable after assignment, merge, split, alias, correction, or decomposition.
clustering.atomicity: A cluster represents one incident. A source record containing multiple separable incidents is retained as a decomposed parent and produces immutable child candidates. If safe decomposition is not possible, disposition is unresolved-multi-incident and it is excluded from scoring.

allowedOnlyWhen: an immutable source incident identifier exactly matches and assessed actor, action, target, location, and incident time do not conflict
normalizationVersion and normalizedContentHash exactly match under crucix-session15-conservative-normalization/v1 and no assessed incident field conflicts

clustering.ambiguousJoin: Persist a proposal and require assisted-human-confirmed or human disposition. No unrecorded model decision is valid.
clustering.tieOrderConstraint: Lexical ordering makes recorded equal-evidence choices reproducible; it never converts unresolved evidence into a high-confidence match.
clustering.nonReuse: Event-cluster and parent-series IDs are stable opaque identifiers and are never reused.

lifecycle.lastMaterialChangeAt: Maximum reliable timestamp among the cluster's persisted material lifecycle transitions. It is not the latest mention or observation time.
lifecycle.materialChange: A persisted change to action stage, operational scope, direct mechanism, correction state, or explicit de-escalation supported by evidence.
lifecycle.nonMaterialRepeat: Repeated coverage without a material change can update lastObservedAt but cannot update lastMaterialChangeAt.
chronologyInvariants: firstSeen must be less than or equal to lastObservedAt
lastMaterialChangeAt must be between firstSeen and lastObservedAt inclusive
lifecycleHistory effectiveAt values and transitionVersion values must be strictly monotonic
a continuing transition is nonmaterial and cannot change lastMaterialChangeAt
new, escalating, and de-escalating transitions are material and require explicit materialTransitionProvenanceId
lifecycle.noDecayOrExpiry: Continuing clusters remain visible in the registry but do not elevate without a recorded material transition. No time-based decay, expiry, stale interval, or inferred de-escalation exists in 2.0.0.

structuralRequirements: event type assessed as one of the five leaves
at least one assessed direct mechanism maps to the channel
signalSelection.announcedHandling: Announced, rhetoric, and threatened events remain visible but are non-elevating.
signalSelection.contribution: A qualifying event cluster contributes at most once to a channel in a run, regardless of candidate count, mechanism count, or report count.
signalSelection.ranking: Within each channel, sort qualifying clusters by action-stage ordinal descending and eventClusterId ascending. Expose all clusters tied on action-stage ordinal; the ID key selects a deterministic leader only.
